How can the U.S. Coast Guard make its waterways safety risk assessment tools work better together?

New report: bit.ly/41PNDMg

RAND experts interviewed state education agency leaders to examine what forms of support from the Department of Education have been more or less useful, and how investments could better address states' needs: bit.ly/4vs5Jle

A retirement plan like the one President Trump recently outlined would not only give workers a cushion for retirement. With enough time, it could also start winding back the federal deficit. bit.ly/3PL9qC4

In a world with AGI, humanity must preserve its survival, capacity for agency, and strategic optionality.

That will require an ecosystem where humans and AI coexist while retaining human agency—and a global security architecture to support it.

New paper: bit.ly/4vmVLS7

Recent policy reforms in Austin, Texas, made it easier to build housing. The result: Construction picked up, home prices and rents came down.

This may provide lessons for other parts of the country, says RAND's Jason Ward. bit.ly/4bWQLuD

There is significant uncertainty surrounding China's national security decisionmaking processes, especially in real time during a crisis or conflict.

This primer can help reduce U.S. misperceptions about Chinese decisionmaking: bit.ly/4mt0TQI
New RAND research can help the U.S. Coast Guard evaluate its existing waterway risk assessment tools. bit.ly/4sgfika
The U.S. Department of Education has historically played an important role in supporting state education agencies. What types of technical support do states value most? bit.ly/3PZV15b

Two Russian satellites have been secretly stalking European spacecraft since the initial invasion of Ukraine in 2014.

What can Europe do to confront this threat? bit.ly/3QguDE1

In a future with AGI, humanity can survive and retain its agency if it builds two interdependent structures:

🔸 an ecosystem where humans and AIs coexist
🔸 a global security architecture that makes this ecosystem possible.

New paper: bit.ly/3PEIKmA

Why are home prices so unaffordable? What reforms could help address the problem? Is California's housing crisis a bellwether for the rest of the country?

New Q&A with RAND's Jason Ward: bit.ly/4bTTN2J

"We've accumulated [the federal] debt over the last 50-plus years. It's going to take us 30-plus years to get out of it. Steps like these proposed retirement accounts, where you shift costs and take advantage of the market, are one way we could get there." bit.ly/3PIMHGQ

"Not only are lower- and middle-income people leaving California, but you see a lot of higher-earning, highly educated people leaving to have a much higher quality of life in places like Texas. It's going to create a brain and service drain." sacbee.com/entertainment/liv…
New paper can help channel polarized debates about the future of AGI into the development of concrete strategies that help humanity survive and preserve agency: bit.ly/4c15NiW

"Any Russian space operation should be seen as part of a larger campaign to accrue strategic benefits, whether to gain a military advantage over Ukraine or to coerce European countries into withdrawing their support for Ukraine." bit.ly/41a9yh6
How can the U.S. Coast Guard make its waterway safety tools work better together? bit.ly/4sd8Ev5

The U.S. faces a historic housing crisis, but RAND's Jason Ward is hopeful about the future.

Find out why in this new Q&A. bit.ly/4uYRh3N

What can Europe do to address aggressive actions by Russia in space?

Aleix Nadal Campos of @RANDEurope discusses: bit.ly/4m4jhyS

Any AGI strategy, whether it favors acceleration or caution, "must demonstrate that it preserves a sufficient level of human agency and choice to, at minimum, allow course correction."

New paper: bit.ly/482IR1u

"There's a lot of interest right now in housing affordability, a lot of momentum for policy changes. Our main priority is to make the most of this opening to produce some helpful, credible, and timely research." bit.ly/4tla8EM
